spatial_claims.claim: C lies on segment AB between A and B, with AC being the greater segment and CB the lesser (AC > CB)
D lies on segment AB between A and B, with AD = DB = AB/2 (D is the midpoint of AB)
AB is divided into two segments AC and CB at point C (used for Prop. 2.2)
AB is divided into two segments AD and DB at point D (used for Prop. 2.1)
A new line of length AC + AD is formed by placing segments of length AC and AD end to end (used for Prop. 2.4)
AB is composed of two equal segments AD and DB (used for Prop. 2.4)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single line segment AB. Point C divides AB in extreme and mean ratio with AC the greater segment (AC approx 0.618*AB). Point D is the midpoint of AB (AD = 0.5*AB). Since AC > AD, the order on the line is A---D---C---B. No triangles, circles, angles, or interior/exterior regions are involved. The proof constructs an auxiliary line of length AC + AD for application of Prop. 2.4, but this is a standard construction with no spatial conflict. The entire proof is algebraic manipulation of area relations from Book 2 and proportions from Book 6.
pass_reason: The proof is essentially algebraic, using Book 2 area identities (2.1, 2.2, 2.4) and Book 6 proportion results (6.17) to derive the result. The only spatial claims are that C and D lie on segment AB in the order A-D-C-B, which is consistent with AC being the greater segment of the golden ratio division and D being the midpoint. There are no angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, no ray orderings, and no geometric configuration that could produce a contradiction. All spatial claims are mutually consistent.
